role: assembly layer: it owns no new original bytes, it wires the sixteen recovered segment/glue modules into the complete spSkeletonJson_readSkeletonData and closes the seven error tails those modules report as codes

functions.name: spSkeletonJson_readSkeletonData
functions.semantics: Single-chain loader: locale guard -> Json_create -> spSkeletonData_create -> meta -> bones -> slots -> ik -> transform -> path -> skins/dispatch/glue/parsers -> linkedmesh postpass -> events -> animations (B1/B2 per-animation loop) -> Json_dispose(root) -> return data. Every stage is its own recovered module; this file owns the order, the root/data lifetimes and the seven error tails reported as codes.
functions.returns: spSkeletonData* on success (root already disposed) or NULL on any segment error (data disposed by the owning tail, root disposed inside setError unless that tail passed root=0)
instruction_anchors: 0x28e7a4 ldr r0,[sp,#0x24] ; 0x28e7a8 bl Json_dispose ; 0x28e7ac mov r0,r9

functions.name: tail_ik_bone_not_found
functions.semantics: spSkeletonData_dispose(data) -> _spSkeletonJson_setError(self, root, "IK bone not found: ", name) -> NULL; r0 comes from the explicitly zeroed r10

functions.name: tail_parent_bone_not_found
functions.census: segment_chain_map.md §5.2 gap 2 (inside the ik window, belongs to bones)
functions.semantics: dispose(data) -> setError(self, root, "Parent bone not found: ", parent name) -> NULL. The parent name is recovered by re-walking the same bone child list with the same findBone lookup (bones are appended in order and never removed, so the first miss of the re-walk is the failing index).

functions.name: tail_locale_fallback
functions.semantics: When setlocale(LC_NUMERIC,NULL) returns NULL the original sets "C", runs Json_create and then resets the locale to NULL without restoring. The entry module cannot report `saved`, so the assembly probes once, installs "C" before entry runs and resets after it.

functions.name: tail_transform_bone_not_found
functions.semantics: dispose(data) -> setError(self, root, "Transform bone not found: ", name) -> NULL

functions.name: tail_path_bone_not_found
functions.semantics: dispose(data) -> setError(self, root, "Path bone not found: ", name) -> NULL

functions.name: tail_invalid_skeleton_json
functions.semantics: Json_create failure: Json_getError() -> setError(self, 0-at-that-point, "Invalid skeleton JSON: ", err) -> NULL; data was never created

functions.name: tail_unknown_attachment_type
functions.census: physically inside the animations address range, so census §5.1 (which stops at 0x28d19c) does not list it; animations_segment_map.md §1.3 already assigns these out-of-line attachment tails to the attachment window and no module claims this one
functions.semantics: dispatch fall-through 0x28c79c bne 0x28e7f4: dispose(data) -> setError(self, root, "Unknown attachment type: ", type) -> NULL

chain_level_state: 0x28bdd8 ldr r8,[sp,#0x28] (json restore at the ik head) and 0x28ccb4 mov r9,r11 (data restore at the skins exit) are C locals here, emitted once
0x28bdcc..0x28bdd4 is the single shared epilogue: one C return, never duplicated per segment
the skins loop constants ("default"/"name"/"path"/"type", 0x55555556) stay inside spine_read_skins / spine_read_attach_dispatch and are never re-loaded here
json->scale is re-read at every scaling site (vldr s15,[r8]) and never cached across calls
frame->animation is set from B2's return (0x28d2c8 str r4,[sp,#0x1c]); the rest of the B3/B4 frame slice is zeroed because B3/B4 write every word before reading it
quirks_preserved: bones key missing -> readSkeletonData_bonesArray dereferences NULL (census §1.4C): no guard was added
bonesCount / skinsCount are running counters; slots/ik/transform/path counts are pre-written from the Json size
the setlocale(NULL) fallback never restores the previous locale
linkedmesh "Skin not found" and "Parent mesh not found" pass root = 0, so the parsed tree LEAKS on those two paths (asserted as a leak, not repaired)
createAttachment returning NULL with no loader error silently drops the attachment and still advances
the three "Target ..." tails load their message argument through r4 = the failed lookup result (0), a latent NULL-page fault on paths the shipped data never takes

returns_contract.success: data, root disposed exactly once by B18
returns_contract.failure: NULL, data disposed once by the owning tail, root disposed once inside setError, json->error holds the formatted text
returns_contract.exception: linkedmesh Skin/Parent-mesh tails: data disposed once, root leaked

synthetic_boundaries: Json_create 0x287320 and Json_getError 0x2872b8 (the parser entry; the fixture returns the staged tree and records the parse-error text)

spBoneData_create 0x285ac8, spSlotData_create 0x28ef6c, spSlotData_setAttachmentName 0x28efd4, spIkConstraintData_create 0x28671c, spTransformConstraintData_create 0x28f5b8, spPathConstraintData_create 0x288ee0
spSkeletonData_findSlot 0x28b070 (92 B in .dynsym; no module in this tree recovered it)
spAnimation_create, spEventData_create, spEvent_create, every timeline create/setFrame, spCurveTimeline_setStepped/setCurve

the fixture heap/allocator rosters, libc providers, hand-built Json nodes
open: The [sp,#0x24] root slot has no carrier in spine_read_entry's C ABI (it returns the "skeleton" child), and a Json tree has no parent link, so the assembly exposes one word, readSkeletonData_rootSlot, that the Json_create provider publishes. A real (unrecovered) Json_create must write it; until then a provider that does not leaves the loader reporting "Invalid skeleton JSON".
spSkeletonData_findSlot 0x28b070 is a .dynsym symbol that no module recovered; the fixture supplies a same-shaped linear scan (count +0x18, table +0x1c, name +0x04).
The locale fallback probe repeats one read-only setlocale(LC_NUMERIC,NULL) call on the normal path; it changes no state, but the original calls it once.
readSkeletonData_metadata takes the tree and re-looks up "skeleton", so the chain performs that lookup twice where the original performs it once (module ABI, not this layer).

The three glue "Target ..." tails read [r0+0x1c] with r0 = 0 (a latent fault). The assembly hands the block a record whose +0x1c is the target name the segment reported, so the block still runs from its owner but the fault itself is not reproduced.

Error tails dispose a data record whose count was published before the array was filled; the fixture pre-points those arrays at inert records so the dispose order/report/root release stay observable. The original's behaviour on real malloc garbage there is UNPROVEN.
A skeleton JSON without a "bones" key dereferences NULL inside readSkeletonData_bonesArray (original quirk, untestable without a fault harness).
Original bytes were never executed and no equivalence measurement exists (axis 4 = not_measured).
